findings.title: A runner-signed session transaction carrying a governance proposal, a certificate, a vote or a non-direct withdrawal: no test fails without it
findings.scenario: refuseOddities' staking/governance clause is all that stops the runner signing such a transaction. A swap Minswap's aggregator builds, or a cancel, could carry a proposal procedure, whose deposit takes no signature and goes back later to a reward address the builder picks (shared/rpc.ts `proposals`), or a witness-free certificate. withinFunding counts only outputs paid to others plus the fee, never a deposit, so a large session's order swap could put part of its funding into a proposal deposit (100,000 ADA on mainnet), with the order made smaller to match. The clause is there. But in all 194 test files that reach sessions.ts, no session transaction has certificates, withdrawals off the direct path, votes or proposals, so deleting the clause passes every test. who: Minswap's aggregator, a third party handing the session a transaction to sign; `site` is the nearest of the five actors.
findings.since: e7d411ee (chunk 15b, 2026-09-24, before the first web-wallet tag); its proposals clause became `s.proposals.length` in ce53ba62 (web-wallet/1.7.2)
findings.evidence: Change (sessions.ts:6867): `if (s.certificates.length || (s.withdrawals.length && !allow.direct) || s.votes || s.proposals.length) {` -> `if (false) {`. Probe pass in a separate copy: the condition wrapped in a logging call that returns its value unchanged, then all 194 test files whose imports reach sessions.ts/parts.ts/collateral.ts/runs.ts run once (2,493 passed, 4 skipped, 0 failed). The probe never logged true in any test. Combined mutant (this one plus 10 other unreached mutants of sessions.ts, applied at once) over the union of their named test files (18 files): 430 passed, and 6 timed out under load (load average 60-85). Those 6 were re-run under the same mutant with their limits raised, and all passed. withinFunding (sessions.ts:6571-6583) sums only `paid` and `fee`.
findings.fix: Add a case to sessions.test.ts beside 'pauses rather than sign a swap that gives ADA to the treasury'. Its swapTx fixture gets a proposal procedure, and in other runs a stake registration certificate, a vote, or a withdrawal on the order path. Expect `paused` {why: 'refused'} with sess.refuse.warn.staking's words, and t.koios.submitted at length 1 (the funding only). Add one for the wallet's own cancel (of = 'cancel') too.
findings.known_check: Searched docs/backlog.md and docs/archive/plans/ for refuseOddities, sess.refuse.warn.staking, 'no test', unpinned and proposals. refuseOddities appears only as design in chunk-15b-swap-runner.md and chunk-24-dapp-additions.md. review-1.7.2.md's proposal items concern a site's sign window, not this check. findings.title: A fee-sized output carrying the session's tokens taken as Minswap's fee: no test fails without it
findings.scenario: In checkOrder, the one output that may be Minswap's fee must be ADA alone (`!o.tokens`). Without that, in a swap selling a token, Minswap's transaction could add an output to any address holding no more ADA than the quoted aggregator fee plus some of the session's tokens. checkOrder would take it as the fee, and withinFunding bounds only the total tokens paid out to the funded amount, a check no test pins either (t1h#3). So tokens meant for the order could go to that output instead. No test builds a fee-sized output that carries tokens.
findings.since: by web-wallet/1.6.0 (line last changed in ab5695a3, 2026-09-27, 'Minswap's fee may go to a contract')
findings.evidence: Change (sessions.ts:6697): `if (!fee && !o.tokens && o.lovelace <= aggregatorFee) {` -> `if (!fee && o.lovelace <= aggregatorFee) {`. Probe: `!o.tokens` wrapped (evaluated only once no fee has been taken). In the 194 related test files it was never false, so no fee candidate in any test carries tokens. Solo mutant run on sessions.test.ts, the lane's named file: 60 passed and 1 timed out at its own 30 s limit. That test, 'pauses rather than sign a swap that pays anyone but the session, an order made out to it, and Minswap's quoted fee', was re-run under the mutant with its limit raised to 600 s, and it passed.
findings.fix: In sessions.test.ts 'pauses rather than sign a swap that pays anyone but the session…', add a swapTx whose extra output holds 1,000,000 lovelace (the quoted fee) plus some of the MIN token. Expect 'it pays an address that isn't this session's.' and nothing signed.

findings.title: A second fee-sized output taken as Minswap's fee: no test fails without it

Without that, Minswap's transaction could pay several outputs to any addresses, each holding up to the quoted aggregator fee, and every one would pass as the fee. withinFunding still caps the ADA paid out at the funding, so the extra fees come out of the funded costs and the session gets less back. No test has two fee-sized outputs.

findings.title: A session transaction that mints or burns: no test fails without it
findings.scenario: refuseOddities alone refuses a swap or cancel whose body mints or burns. withinFunding counts only tokens paid to others, so a burn under a policy anyone may run (an always-succeeding script) could destroy tokens at the session's account without counting as paid. Since no session transaction in the tests has a mint field, deleting the check passes every test.
findings.evidence: Change (sessions.ts:6870): `if (s.mint.length) throw new Refused(t("sess.refuse.warn.mints"), of);` -> `` (deleted). Probe: `s.mint.length` was never non-zero in any of the 194 related test files. Combined-mutant run as in t1h#1: all pass.

findings.title: A stranger's exactly-5-ADA UTxO carrying tokens put up as a chain's collateral: no test fails without it
findings.scenario: Anyone can pay a session's one-time account, including exactly 5 ADA plus tokens. The chain takes its funding's own 5 ADA first (sessions.ts:4625), and any fitting UTxO only once that one is gone, for example after a site's transaction or an earlier return spent it. collateralFits' `!u.asset_list?.length` is what keeps the stranger's token-carrying 5 ADA from standing in. No test puts a 5 ADA UTxO with tokens at a session's account, so the clause can go with every test passing. The clause's siblings for a reference script and an inline datum are pinned. What the chain would do with a token-carrying collateral is untested either way.
findings.since: by web-wallet/1.6.0 (10f19f40, 2026-09-27, 'a return's chain never puts up a stranger's 5 ADA carrying a datum')
findings.evidence: Change (sessions.ts:1053): ` && !u.asset_list?.length` removed from `return BigInt(u.value) === SESSION_COLLATERAL && !u.asset_list?.length && …`. Probe: the token test, evaluated only for exactly-5-ADA rows, was never true in any of the 194 related test files. Combined-mutant run over session-collateral.test.ts, lovejoin.test.ts and 16 more: all pass (430, plus the 6 re-run after load timeouts).
findings.fix: Add a case to session-collateral.test.ts like 'says why when the only 5 ADA there carries a datum'. Spend the session's own 5 ADA (t.koios.spent.add of its outpoint), and unshift a stranger's 5 ADA with an asset_list entry. Expect backBuild's review to have no lovejoin and lovejoinSkipped matching /5 ADA collateral isn't at its account/.

findings.title: A stranger's 5 ADA with a datum by hash put up as a chain's collateral: no test fails without it

findings.title: A second 'Mix my boxes again' sent while one may still spend the same boxes: no test fails without the Send-time check
findings.scenario: againBuild refuses a second again-mix once one is recorded (sessions.ts:2208, pinned by lovejoin.test.ts). Review isn't in the queue, though. One built while the first one's Send is still recording passes that check, and its kept review then replaces the first's. At Send, only mixOutSubmit's own check stops its session being recorded and its funding sent beside a chain that spends the same boxes. Only one of the two chains can take them, and the other session's money waits to come back, with fees. No test builds a second again-mix that overlaps the first's Send.

findings.title: A top-up review older than BUILT_TTL_MS recorded before Send refuses it: no test fails without it
findings.scenario: topUpSubmit refuses a top-up reviewed more than 10 minutes ago before recording anything. Without that, the top-up would go into the session's record (outRecord, update). Then send()'s own age check (script-spend.ts:393-395) would refuse it, and markUnsent would mark it unsent: a turned-away top-up in the session's record, and possibly the other message. No money moves either way. No test sends a top-up past its review's age.

findings.title: A funding or top-up that Koios answered with another transaction's id marked never sent: no test fails without markUnsent's maybe-sent exception
findings.scenario: markUnsent keeps a failed funding or top-up 'on its way' when Koios didn't answer it (maybeSent) or a lock cut it off. The lock half is pinned. The maybe-sent half can only fire on one path: submitWatched turns every unanswered submit into a maybe-sent return, never a throw (pending.ts:478), so the only maybe-sent error that reaches markUnsent is otherTxId (pending.ts:496-500), raised when Koios's submit answers with a different transaction's id. Marked unsent, such a funding would show as failed, and Forget could drop a record whose funding may land. No test has Koios answer another id.
findings.evidence: Change (sessions.ts:3030): `if (maybeSent(e) || e instanceof WalletLocked) return;` -> `if (e instanceof WalletLocked) return;`. Probe: maybeSent(e) was never true here in any of the 194 related test files (the WalletLocked half was, in sessions-sent-twice.test.ts). Every KoiosBusyError is thrown at a submit (koios.ts:1199-1282, data-layer.ts:405-418) or on another id (pending.ts:500, sessions.ts:5614). Combined-mutant run as in t1h#1 (the lane-less guard's 10 candidate files included): all pass. The lock half's mutant is caught by sessions-sent-twice.test.ts 'Send again on a funding that went out never marks a funding Koios took unsent when the wallet locks…'.
findings.fix: Add a sessions-sent-twice.test.ts case where the fake Koios submitTx returns another transaction's id for a session's funding. Expect the funding to have no `unsent`, the session not to show as failed, and forget to refuse it.
findings.known_check: Searched docs/backlog.md and docs/archive/plans/ for markUnsent, otherTxId and 'another id': nothing.

findings.title: A swap signed when WebAssembly answers its cancel dry run for fewer orders than asked: no test fails without the length check
findings.scenario: cancelsChecked runs each order's cancel in WebAssembly (checkOrderCancels) before the swap is signed, so Stop can always bring the money back. `checked.length !== orders.length` refuses an answer covering fewer orders than asked: `every` over an empty answer is true. Only a WebAssembly bug could give such an answer, and no test fakes one.
findings.since: 5f7a405a (2026-10-08, the 1.3.0 release review's fixes; before the first web-wallet tag)
findings.evidence: Change (sessions.ts:4288): `if (checked.length !== orders.length || !checked.every(cancels)) {` -> `if (!checked.every(cancels)) {`. Probe: the length test was never true in any of the 194 related test files. Combined-mutant run as in t1h#1 (order-cancel-check.test.ts included): all pass. The rest of the check is pinned: without the whole condition, or the fee cap, order-cancel-check.test.ts fails.
findings.fix: Add an order-cancel-check.test.ts case wrapping deps.wasm.checkOrderCancels to return { orders: [] }. Expect the swap paused with sess.refuse.warn.notCancellable's words, and nothing signed.
findings.known_check: Searched docs/backlog.md and docs/archive/plans/ for checkOrderCancels and notCancellable. chunk-47 mentions checkOrderCancels as automatic. Nothing about the length check.

findings.title: A session swap or cancel sent whose signed bytes don't hash to the transaction inspected: no test fails without either check
findings.scenario: signAndSend has two checks: that the signer's summary hash (sessions.ts:4477) and the witnessed bytes' id (4481) equal the txHash the checks passed. Together they keep the session's key from sending a transaction other than the one inspected: a kept request that no longer matches its body, or a witness set that changes the body. With the real WebAssembly the hashes always agree, and no test fakes a signer or attachWitnesses that changes the body, so both can be deleted with every test passing.
findings.since: e7d411ee (chunk 15b, 2026-09-24) for 4477; 4481 by web-wallet/1.6.0 (line last changed in e90efff5)
findings.evidence: Changes, each its own mutant: (a) sessions.ts:4477 `if (signed.summary.txHash !== built.txHash) throw new Error(t("worker.spend.signingChanged"));` -> `` (deleted); (b) sessions.ts:4481 `if (txId(bytes) !== built.txHash) throw new Error(t("sess.witnessChanged"));` -> `` (deleted). Probes: both conditions were only ever false in the 194 related test files, and no test contains witnessChanged or signingChanged. Combined-mutant run with both deleted, over sessions, swap-runner, direct-swaps, order-cancel-check, sundae-orders, pool-swap-landing and 12 more: all pass (430, plus the 6 load timeouts re-run).
findings.fix: Add a sessions.test.ts case for each check. One wraps deps.wasm.signSessionTx to return a summary with another txHash. The other wraps attachWitnesses to return other body bytes. Each expects the runner's step to fail with that check's words and t.koios.submitted to hold only the funding.
findings.known_check: Searched docs/backlog.md and docs/archive/plans/ for signingChanged and witnessChanged: no mentions.

notes: Method. Each sub-check is its own mutant: 140 mutants over the 50 unique guards (E2a#11 = E2b#19). Phase 1 on the named tests was too slow under the machine's load (average 40-85 from every T1 lane), so after two runs (a03, a22) the work switched to probes. In a separate copy, every guard's condition was wrapped in a logging call that returns its value unchanged. All 194 test files whose import graph reaches sessions.ts, parts.ts, collateral.ts or runs.ts then ran once: 2,493 passed, 4 skipped, 0 failed, so the probes changed nothing. Each mutant then ran against the tests where its guard fires (named files first, -t and --bail=1). 127 were caught. The 12 that no test reaches were confirmed by one combined run of all of them over the union of their named files, plus b01ft alone. a11h, reached but never decisive, also ran its file whole.

Load noise, handled in the copies only: the per-test default timeout was raised to 30 s (from Vitest's 5 s), and failures that were timeouts alone never counted as caught. Three tests that set their own limits (sessions.test.ts:1277 30 s, lovejoin.test.ts:895 120 s, dapp.test.ts:368 30 s) timed out under load and were re-run under the same mutant with those limits raised. That turned b01n from a timeout into a catch, and confirmed the combined run and b01ft as passing.

The lanes' 'none found' guards: E2a#3 is pinned by sessions.test.ts, E2a#23 by collateral.test.ts and lovejoin-planner.test.ts, and E2a#24 by run-traps-review-fixes.test.ts. E2a#22's lock half is pinned by sessions-sent-twice.test.ts; its maybe-sent half (t1h#10) and E2b#11 (t1h#12) aren't.

Named tests that never reach their guard, per the probes: sessions-refused.test.ts (named for E2a#0) imports only a type from shared/rpc and never loads sessions.ts. payment-forms.test.ts likewise touches no guarded module. session-index.test.ts never has freshIndex meet a used index (E2a#2 is pinned by restore-scan.test.ts). site-funding-seen.test.ts and parts-send-review-fixes.test.ts never reach fundingState's two cases (E2a#12). parts-send-review-fixes.test.ts never makes partsMayGo refuse (E2b#17). restore-scan.test.ts and session-top-up-again.test.ts never reach topUpSubmit's sent-already or stale checks (E2a#8). sessions.test.ts never reaches act's ownGone and ordersOpen holds (E2b#13), refuseOddities' other-key and keys checks (E2b#6), or checkOrder's unreadable and stake-signed checks (E2b#1). Each is pinned elsewhere, as listed in guards. E2a#4's recent half is reached by the named session-top-up-again.test.ts, which passes without it; sessions.test.ts pins it.

Caught only by wording: removing these still leaves the transaction refused, by a later check or a crash, and the test fails only because the reason differs. checkOrder's b01k, b01f, b01a and b01c (another clause, or withinFunding, refuses the same transaction); refuseParts b14 and fundingChange b16 (reserve() still refuses, as 'Lovejoin's pool changed'); directSpends' unknown input b02u and topUpSubmit's stale check a08r (a TypeError instead of the refusal). A rewording that kept the tests' strings in step would hide their removal.

For the owner: the most consequential gap is t1h#1. withinFunding never counts a deposit, so for a swap that runs itself, refuseOddities' proposal/certificate clause alone keeps Minswap's build from moving part of a large funding into a governance proposal deposit returned to a reward address of the builder's choosing. The clause is present; only its test is missing. The token side of an order swap's check (t1h#2, t1h#3) is similarly untested end to end.
Not in E2a's or E2b's lists, so not tried: order()'s own route refusals (sessions.ts:4146-4151), swapBuild's (3203-3207), and sendChain's chain-on-its-way check (5174).

Nothing was written into TREE. TREE's one modified tracked file, review-51/INDEX.md, isn't mine. The copies (mutant, probe, combined) were removed. No Rust was built: none of these guards is in Rust. Vitest wrote its results cache into the shared node_modules/.vite, as the brief's symlink setup does for every T1 lane.
coverage: All 50 unique guards in E2a's and E2b's lists were tried: E2a's 25 and E2b's 26, with E2a#11 and E2b#19 merged. Every sub-check a lane named by line or clause is a mutant of its own, 140 in all, each in a copy, never in TREE. Every mutant has a verdict: 127 caught and 13 not caught. The 13 fall under 9 lane guards: E2a#8, E2a#11/E2b#19, E2a#19, E2a#22, E2b#0, E2b#1, E2b#6, E2b#8 and E2b#11. They are reported as 12 findings, since both signAndSend checks are one. No guard was left untried. Run scope: phase 1 ran a03 and a22 against their named or candidate files. Every other mutant ran against the tests the probes show its guard firing in, out of the 194 test files whose imports reach the four guarded modules. All 194 ran once with probes. The unreached ones were confirmed by a combined run over their named files. a11h also ran its one reaching file whole without -t. The whole suite wasn't run per mutant: tests the probes show never reaching a guard can't see its mutant. Load timeouts were re-run with raised limits, as the notes describe. Not tried: Rust and WebAssembly guards (none in these lists), and the route checks outside the lanes' lines.
